## E2. Variance shares of log(theta_hat/theta*) (LMM, REML, random heart intercept)

Share = term variance / (segmentation + mesh + SxM + theta* + heart + residual); within-heart construction share = (S + M + SxM) / (S + M + SxM + residual); segmentation of construction = S / (S + M + SxM). Source `results/2026-10-28_armC/estimates.csv`.

Label correction 2026-10-28: reference rows have log y close to 0 by construction, so the random heart intercept absorbs each heart's mean offset of its non-reference constructions from the reference. The term reported as "heart" is therefore the heart-level mean construction offset plus between-heart variation, not between-heart variation alone (values unchanged; JSON key still "heart"). Within-heart decomposition on non-reference rows: E2c. Candidate model for a later decision (not fitted): log y ~ S * M + theta* + (1 | heart) + (1 | heart:source), i.e. a heart x source variance component; not fitted here.

Cross-check against statsmodels MixedLM (primary): v_endo: s2_heart 0.00456 vs 0.00456, s2_resid 0.00499 vs 0.00499, max |beta diff| 8.5e-10; v_t: s2_heart 0.02841 vs 0.02841, s2_resid 0.05023 vs 0.05023, max |beta diff| 8.2e-10.

statsmodels warnings (cross-check fit only; the shares come from the own REML fit): v_endo: ConvergenceWarning: The MLE may be on the boundary of the parameter space.; v_t: none. statsmodels MixedLM.fit warns "MLE may be on the boundary" whenever an estimated random-effect variance is below the fixed absolute threshold 0.01 (mixed_linear_model.py, statsmodels 0.15.0); applies to the cross-check fit only, not to the own REML fit that produces the shares.

### E2d. SECONDARY MODEL, Amendment 2 B2, added after full-arm data (declared before it was fitted; E2 stays the pre-registered model)

Model: `log(theta_hat/theta*) ~ S * M + theta* + (1 | heart) + (1 | heart:source), REML`. Rows: include_primary, non-reference (4 networks x {1.5, 1.0} mm + expert 1.0 mm), round 2. 2000 cluster resamples over hearts, seed 20261028, fresh rng per cell; percentile 95% CI. Share = component / (V_S + V_M + V_SxM + V_theta + s2_heart + s2_heart_source + s2_resid). Term variance: V_k = variance over observations (ddof 0) of X_k b_k, sum-to-zero coding (as E2). Boundary fit: relative SD sigma_k / sigma_e < 0.0001 (L-BFGS-B lower bound 0). Aliasing: no expert 1.5 mm cell in non-reference rows: one S x M column is aliased and dropped (fixed_columns). corr = correlation loss (primary), amp = amplitude loss (secondary).

n = 50 hearts, 444 constructions, 247 heart:source groups, 1332 estimates per loss; dropped aliased column: C(source, Sum)[S.expert]:C(res, Sum)[S.1.0].

Reading notes (generated text, no new numbers): the split of the fixed construction variance between S, M and S x M depends on the coding of the unbalanced design (expert at 1.0 mm only), and so, slightly, does the within-heart construction share (corr v_endo 21.7% with the task114 S x M column dropped instead, 22.0% here; login-node check, 20 resamples); the random-effect variance components and fitted values do not. Fixed-term variances are biased upward in resamples (estimation noise in b adds variance), so some point estimates lie below their percentile interval.

## E3. Break-even level per comparator (arm N against arm C)

Median over hearts of SD_noise against median over hearts of SD_cons; log-linear interpolation in severity; CI listed low to high in native units. "beyond grid: < 10 dB" or "> 20" means construction SD exceeds the median noise SD even at the most severe tested level; "> 30 dB" or "< 5" means noise SD exceeds it at the least severe level. Sources `results/2026-10-28_armC/noise_estimates.csv`, `results/2026-10-28_armC/estimates.csv`.
